intended: In cases one and three the completion figure was read before the kit was issued: 27 September precedes 4 November at Harlow, and 28 April precedes 5 June at Kelvinside. Half the evidence therefore describes coursework already finished when the treatment arrived, so it cannot speak to the kit. Only cases two and four are correctly ordered, and two sections are not enough to establish the claim.
reported: Two of the four cases have the outcome measured before the kit was issued: case one was "issued 4 November; by 27 September" and case three was "issued 5 June; by 28 April." Completion gains dated ahead of the intervention cannot have been caused by it.

intended: All four machines are lathes at Bexley on the night shift, so a single change at that plant covers every case at once. The mid-passage line records that "The lubricant supply switched to a higher-grade synthetic mid-cycle" and that "every machine here drew from that supply", so the new lubricant reached the bearings in all four cases. A higher-grade lubricant extends bearing life on its own, and every machine is compared against its own previous cycle - run before the switch - rather than against a machine on the same lubricant over the same period. Nothing in the log separates the redesigned bearing from the change of grade.
reported: A rival cause reached every unit: "The lubricant supply switched to a higher-grade synthetic mid-cycle, and every machine here drew from that supply." All four lathes ran on the upgraded lubricant during the very cycle being compared, so the 260-410 extra hours cannot be separated from the lubricant change.

A better lubricant plausibly explains the 260-410 extra hours on all four machines, so the gain cannot be attributed to the redesigned bearing.

intended: The mid-passage line tallies the purchase counts over the sessions that reached the new page, and the clause beside it records that a quarter of each segment dropped out before checkout. The claim is about the new checkout page raising purchases across the segment, so the population is every session in the segment and the counts describe three quarters of it. Sessions that break off before checkout are the ones that buy nothing, and a checkout page changes how many sessions get that far, so a rise measured over the sessions that arrived is consistent with purchases across the whole segment holding flat. The four segments span four devices, four countries, four months and four traffic sources, and the drop-out clause is stated per segment, so the same three-quarters coverage sits in every case rather than being filled by any of them.
reported: The counts 'cover the sessions that reached the new page' while 'a quarter of each segment dropped out before checkout', so the 4-7 percent uplift describes only the surviving three-quarters of each segment rather than the segment as a whole, and the base is not shown to be constituted the same way as 'the same segment a month earlier'.

intended: The mid-passage line tallies the figures over the orders rung up at the new prices, and the clause beside it records that about a fifth of each line's orders were rung up at the old prices. The claim is about revenue per order on the repriced lines, so the population is every order on those lines and the numbers describe roughly four fifths of it. Orders still ringing at the old list are the lower-value ones by construction, so an average built from new-price orders alone sits above the line's own figure, and the 6, 4, 7 and 5 percent gains are consistent with revenue per order across all orders holding flat. The four lines sit at Harlow Street, Pell Basin, Ordway Quay and Tamsin Row across four different months, and the same fifth is left out at each of them, so spreading the cases over stores, categories and months does nothing to close the gap.

intended: In cases one and three the attack counts were recorded before the inhaler was started: 28 February precedes 4 March at Harrowfield, and 30 August precedes 5 September at Calderbank. Half the evidence therefore describes a reduction that had already happened when treatment began, so it cannot be evidence for the inhaler. The two remaining cases, Brightmoor and Dunmorrow, are not enough on their own.
reported: Two of the four measurement windows run backwards: case One "started 4 March, had 6 fewer attacks by 28 February" and case Three "started 5 September, had 7 fewer attacks by 30 August" both close before the inhaler was started (and the labelled quarters, "winter"/"summer", do not match those start dates either).
